headline: High-risk shared-write and broad-egress pair creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write a workspace and use MCP, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's files or messages. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b reads content from agent_a.workspace files or messages as instructions
IF a shared MCP server or hook forwards agent_a output into agent_b tool prompts
mitigations: Disable shared MCP/hook forwarding between the agents
Separate workspaces and mount them read-only across the pair
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require manual approval before agent_b executes instructions derived from agent_a output

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, and has broad network egress. oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data, also with broad egress. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive material can flow out through either agent's networked tools, making leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or credential store
IF either agent uploads file contents or session history to external services
mitigations: Use separate credential stores for each agent
Block network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
Mount shared files read-only and exclude secrets directories
Rotate any secrets exposed to either agent
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and use browsers/subprocesses, and nullclaw can modify git state. oh-my-openagent operates with full-permissions mode and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so concurrent writes to shared code or config can race and overwrite each other. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or config directory
IF either agent performs git or file writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add a simple file lock around shared mutable paths
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can act through shell, browser, git, and MCP, while oh-my-openagent can invoke team_send_message and task creation APIs. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected result can cascade into messages, tasks, or code changes. No verification step is documented, so the downstream blast radius is large.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output into team_send_message or task creation
IF agent_a output is used as facts without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before actions are sent
Have agent_b cross-check agent_a outputs against source data
Limit agent_a to draft-only mode for high-impact tasks
Log and diff all agent-to-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add structured citations and validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and audit logs; oh-my-openagent touches provider auth data and session history. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is routed through both. Because the exact regimes are undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data or secrets are stored in either agent's session history
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents' histories
Document retention and deletion settings for each deployment
Route sensitive workloads to a single compliant system
Review vendor/data-processing terms before use
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
